## Proposal: Set a January 15 Intake Deadline for H-1B Registrations

**For discussion Thursday (Marcus, Rosa)**

Last cap season we filed 14 registrations for 6 employer clients. Nine of those 14 came in during the final week of February. Rosa logged about 11 hours of overtime the week the window opened. We got everything filed, but it was tighter than it needed to be.

Most of that crunch came from our own process. Right now we send the questionnaire whenever an employer asks for it, and we never give anyone a date. Employers didn't drag their feet; they just had nothing to plan around. One HR contact told me she'd have happily sent everything in January if we'd asked. I think that's true for most of our clients.

An earlier date also protects us. The registration is simple, but mistakes are expensive. Brightwater Analytics sent a beneficiary's passport scan two days before the window, and it had expired in October. We only caught it because Rosa checked the dates. A wrong passport means an invalid selection, which is not something we want to discover in the last 48 hours.

January 15 is realistic. HR teams are back from the holidays, Q1 budgets are set, and the $215 per-beneficiary registration fee is already in those budgets. We aren't asking clients for anything new. We're asking for the same things earlier, with clear notice.

**What would change:**

- Engagement letters and the one-page questionnaire go out the week of December 7.
- Intake closes January 15.
- Anything after January 15 is handled case by case. We won't turn anyone away, but the date is the default.
- Rosa, who owns the tracker, gets a clean six weeks before the window opens to chase missing documents, verify passport dates, and fix gaps without overtime.

I'd present this to clients as better service: a clear timeline, earlier review of their documents, and fewer last-minute requests from us. It shouldn't read as a deadline because anyone was late.

**Decision needed Thursday:** if we agree, I'll finalize the December letters so they can go out on schedule.
